entries.title: AI Fundamentals and Responsible Use Manual
entries.snippet: Accessible keyboard-first AI Fundamentals and Responsible Use manual for blind and low-vision learners.
entries.text: ai fundamentals and responsible use manual ai fundamentals and responsible use manual accessible keyboard-first ai fundamentals and responsible use manual for blind and low-vision learners. ai fundamentals and responsible use manual - accessible learning center accessible artificial intelligence foundations ai fundamentals and responsible use manual practical, responsible ai skills for work, learning, and independent problem-solving. basics prompting verification privacy screen readers lessons what generative ai does generative ai predicts and creates text or other content from patterns in training data and the information supplied in a conversation. it can help brainstorm, organize, explain, summarize, and draft. it does not understand a situation the way a person does, and it can produce confident but incorrect or invented information. use ai as an assistant, not as the final decision-maker. a person remains responsible for checking accuracy, appropriateness, accessibility, and compliance with workplace rules. a reliable prompt pattern task: state exactly what you want. context: explain the audience and purpose using nonprivate information. constraints: give length, tone, reading level, deadline, or other limits. format: request headings, bullets, a numbered procedure, or a simple table. checks: ask the tool to identify uncertainty and provide sources when appropriate. continue the conversation with specific follow-ups. for example: “shorten this to 150 words,” “explain the second step,” or “which statements need verification?” verify before using the result open original sources instead of trusting an ai summary or citation. confirm names, dates, quotations, calculations, contact details, laws, policies, and software instructions. prefer current primary sources from the organization responsible for the information. compare important claims with a second reliable source. test instructions safely before giving them to another person. rewrite the final result in your own voice and keep a record of corrections. privacy and workplace rules do not enter client records, medical or disability details, passwords, financial account information, private addresses, confidential workplace material, copyrighted documents you are not permitted to share, or information that identifies another person. use fictional or public information in these lessons. follow the employer’s approved-tool, retention, disclosure, and human-review requirements. a personal free account is not automatically approved for organizational data. never allow ai to make an employment, benefit, medical, legal, financial, safety, or accommodation decision for a person. accessible output ask for descriptive headings, short paragraphs, meaningful link text, numbered steps, and simple tables. ask for image descriptions when an image matters, but verify the description with a trusted person when accuracy is important. avoid layouts that communicate meaning only through color, position, or visual formatting. jaws, narrator, and nvda ai interfaces change often. use tab and shift+tab to move among controls, enter or space to activate a control, and the screen reader’s heading, landmark, link, button, edit-field, and browse-mode commands to review the page. use browser find to locate words such as “sources,” “copy,” or part of your prompt. jaws: h moves by heading, b by button, e by edit field, insert+f7 opens links, and insert+f5 opens form fields. nvda: h moves by heading, b by button, e by edit field, nvda+f7 opens the elements list, and nvda+space switches browse and focus modes. narrator: use caps lock or insert with arrow keys for scan mode navigation; press caps lock+space to toggle scan mode when needed. after sending a prompt, allow time for the response to finish. move by heading or paragraph and confirm whether focus changed. product-specific keyboard behavior may change after updates. free-course rule these lessons can be completed with an available free ai service or by studying the examples without creating an account. do not start a paid trial, enter payment information, or purchase a subscription for this course. official references nist ai risk management framework nist generative ai profile ai fundamentals and responsible use lessons lesson 1: what generative ai can and cannot do lesson 2: write a clear prompt with context and constraints lesson 3: continue a conversation and refine a result lesson 4: verify facts, dates, links, and calculations lesson 5: protect entries.snippet: Accessible BrailleBlaster manual for keyboard and JAWS users.
entries.text: brailleblaster manual brailleblaster accessible manual accessible brailleblaster manual for keyboard and jaws users. brailleblaster manual - accessible learning center accessible technology manual brailleblaster accessible manual a keyboard-first guide for blind and low-vision learners using jaws. all manuals ten brailleblaster lessons my progress purpose and setup this manual supports independent practice with brailleblaster on windows. use the exact software version, device model, account permissions, and workplace policy available to you. commands and labels can change after updates. start jaws before opening the application or connecting a braille device. use insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focus, and insert+1 for keyboard help. practice with fictional, public, instructor-provided, or redacted information only. never submit passwords, recovery codes, government identifiers, protected books, or private workplace data. save a backup before changing, deleting, converting, or remediating a file. ten-lesson learning path lesson 1: interface, open, and save a bbz project — create a project log describing the interface and saved bbz file. lesson 2: navigate source and braille views — submit a navigation reference for the project views. lesson 3: apply headings and structure — structure a short workplace policy with two heading levels. lesson 4: create lists and indented material — format one bulleted and one numbered list. lesson 5: format simple tables — format a simple three-column workplace schedule. lesson 6: page numbers, running heads, and breaks — prepare a two-page practice document with verified numbering. lesson 7: styles, emphasis, and special text — correct inconsistent styles in an instructor-provided sample. lesson 8: math, graphics, and transcriber notes — create a decision log for three special-content examples. lesson 9: proofread, validate, and export brf — submit the final bbz or brf plus a proofreading checklist. lesson 10: final workplace transcription project — produce a complete braille-ready workplace procedure. accessible working routine confirm the window, document, device, or webpage title. identify keyboard focus before typing or activating a control. navigate by real structure—headings, lists, fields, tables, or menus—when available. review the result with jaws or a braille display from beginning to end. verify the destination and filename before saving, uploading, sharing, or deleting. use the course’s private assignment uploader only for the requested practice file. important: these course controls complement, and do not replace, browser, operating-system, screen-reader, braille-display, or other assistive-technology settings. official references use these primary sources when a label or command differs from the lesson: aph brailleblaster brailleblaster documentation start brailleblaster lesson 1 return to manuals brailleblaster manual.html

entries.title: ChatGPT Manual
entries.snippet: Accessible keyboard-first ChatGPT manual for blind and low-vision learners.
entries.text: chatgpt manual chatgpt manual accessible keyboard-first chatgpt manual for blind and low-vision learners. chatgpt manual - accessible learning center accessible chatgpt course chatgpt manual practical, responsible ai skills for work, learning, and independent problem-solving. basics prompting verification privacy screen readers lessons what generative ai does generative ai predicts and creates text or other content from patterns in training data and the information supplied in a conversation. it can help brainstorm, organize, explain, summarize, and draft. it does not understand a situation the way a person does, and it can produce confident but incorrect or invented information. use ai as an assistant, not as the final decision-maker. a person remains responsible for checking accuracy, appropriateness, accessibility, and compliance with workplace rules. a reliable prompt pattern task: state exactly what you want. context: explain the audience and purpose using nonprivate information. constraints: give length, tone, reading level, deadline, or other limits. format: request headings, bullets, a numbered procedure, or a simple table. checks: ask the tool to identify uncertainty and provide sources when appropriate. continue the conversation with specific follow-ups. for example: “shorten this to 150 words,” “explain the second step,” or “which statements need verification?” verify before using the result open original sources instead of trusting an ai summary or citation. confirm names, dates, quotations, calculations, contact details, laws, policies, and software instructions. prefer current primary sources from the organization responsible for the information. compare important claims with a second reliable source. test instructions safely before giving them to another person. rewrite the final result in your own voice and keep a record of corrections. privacy and workplace rules do not enter client records, medical or disability details, passwords, financial account information, private addresses, confidential workplace material, copyrighted documents you are not permitted to share, or information that identifies another person. use fictional or public information in these lessons. follow the employer’s approved-tool, retention, disclosure, and human-review requirements. a personal free account is not automatically approved for organizational data. never allow ai to make an employment, benefit, medical, legal, financial, safety, or accommodation decision for a person. accessible output ask for descriptive headings, short paragraphs, meaningful link text, numbered steps, and simple tables. ask for image descriptions when an image matters, but verify the description with a trusted person when accuracy is important. avoid layouts that communicate meaning only through color, position, or visual formatting. jaws, narrator, and nvda ai interfaces change often. use tab and shift+tab to move among controls, enter or space to activate a control, and the screen reader’s heading, landmark, link, button, edit-field, and browse-mode commands to review the page. use browser find to locate words such as “sources,” “copy,” or part of your prompt. jaws: h moves by heading, b by button, e by edit field, insert+f7 opens links, and insert+f5 opens form fields. nvda: h moves by heading, b by button, e by edit field, nvda+f7 opens the elements list, and nvda+space switches browse and focus modes. narrator: use caps lock or insert with arrow keys for scan mode navigation; press caps lock+space to toggle scan mode when needed. after sending a prompt, allow time for the response to finish. move by heading or paragraph and confirm whether focus changed. product-specific keyboard behavior may change after updates. free-course rule these lessons can be completed with an available free ai service or by studying the examples without creating an account. do not start a paid trial, enter payment information, or purchase a subscription for this course. official references official chatgpt help openai: does chatgpt tell the truth? openai data controls faq chatgpt lessons lesson 1: open chatgpt and navigate the conversation interface lesson 2: write and send an effective first prompt lesson 3: use follow-up prompts to improve an answer lesson 4: create accessible lists, tables, and step-by-step instructions entries.text: chrome lesson 1 chrome lesson 1 accessible google chrome lesson 1: chrome layout, address bar, and basic navigation. chrome lesson 1 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 1 chrome layout, address bar, and basic navigation chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal navigate chrome’s main controls, enter a web address, and move safely through page history. step-by-step instructions open chrome and press ctrl+l to focus the address bar. type https://accessiblelearning.github.io/accessible-learning-center/ and press enter. press alt+left arrow to go back and alt+right arrow to go forward. press alt+home to open the configured home page, then return to the learning site. press ctrl+r to reload the current page. press esc to stop a page that is still loading or dismiss an open browser control. press f6 repeatedly to move among the webpage, address bar, toolbar, and tab strip. with jaws, press insert+t to confirm the window and insert+tab to identify focus. record each command and the browser area it controls. save as chrome-lesson-1.txt. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-1.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting address bar, back, forward, reload, and f6 are explained. the report names the practice site. the student distinguishes browser controls from webpage content. the file is chrome-lesson-1.txt. chrome manual next lesson chrome lesson 1.html

entries.title: Chrome Lesson 10
entries.snippet: Accessible Google Chrome Lesson 10: Final Accessible Workplace Research Project.
entries.text: chrome lesson 10 chrome lesson 10 accessible google chrome lesson 10: final accessible workplace research project. chrome lesson 10 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 10 final accessible workplace research project chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal combine chrome, jaws, research, tabs, bookmarks, forms, and file-safety skills. step-by-step instructions choose a fictional workplace question that can be answered from public information. search for two authoritative sources and open them in separate tabs. use headings, links, lists, and find to locate relevant information. record each page title, organization, address, and publication or update date. compare one fact across both sources. bookmark the strongest source with a meaningful name. locate one form and identify its fields without submitting private information. locate one downloadable file and record its name and type without opening it if unnecessary. write the answer, commands used, accessibility observations, and safety decisions. review with jaws say all and save as chrome-lesson-10.txt. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-10.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting two authoritative sources are documented. at least eight chrome or jaws commands are recorded. a bookmark, form, and potential download are evaluated. no private information is submitted. the file is chrome-lesson-10.txt. chrome manual review my progress chrome lesson 10.html

entries.title: Chrome Lesson 2
entries.snippet: Accessible Google Chrome Lesson 2: Tabs, Windows, and Restoring Work.
entries.text: chrome lesson 2 chrome lesson 2 accessible google chrome lesson 2: tabs, windows, and restoring work. chrome lesson 2 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 2 tabs, windows, and restoring work chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal open, switch, close, reopen, and organize browser tabs and windows. step-by-step instructions press ctrl+t to open a new tab. open a safe practice website from the address bar. press ctrl+tab and ctrl+shift+tab to move forward and backward among tabs. press ctrl+1 through ctrl+8 to move to a numbered tab and ctrl+9 to move to the last tab. press ctrl+w to close only the active tab. press ctrl+shift+t to reopen the most recently closed tab. press ctrl+n to open a new chrome window. use alt+tab to move between chrome windows and other applications. close the extra chrome window with alt+f4 after confirming it is the intended window. write a tab-and-window guide in chrome-lesson-2.txt. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-2.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting tab and window commands are distinguished. closing and reopening a tab are explained. the student confirms windows before closing them. the file is chrome-lesson-2.txt. chrome manual next lesson chrome lesson 2.html

entries.title: Chrome Lesson 3
entries.snippet: Accessible Google Chrome Lesson 3: JAWS Web Navigation in Chrome.
entries.text: chrome lesson 3 chrome lesson 3 accessible google chrome lesson 3: jaws web navigation in chrome. chrome lesson 3 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 3 jaws web navigation in chrome chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal use the jaws virtual cursor, navigation quick keys, and element lists in chrome. step-by-step instructions open the accessible learning center home page. confirm the virtual cursor is on with insert+z; turn it back on if needed. press ctrl+home, then h and shift+h to move by heading. use p for paragraphs, l for lists, and i for list items. press tab and shift+tab to move among links and controls. press insert+f6 to open the headings list. press insert+f7 to open the links list. use insert+ctrl+f for jaws find and compare it with chrome find using ctrl+f. open one lesson link, then use alt+left arrow to return. write the commands and one accessibility observation in chrome-lesson-3.txt. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-3.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting at least eight navigation commands are included. chrome find and jaws find are compared. one helpful page structure feature is identified. the file is chrome-lesson-3.txt. chrome manual next lesson chrome lesson 3.html

entries.title: Chrome Lesson 4
entries.snippet: Accessible Google Chrome Lesson 4: Web Search, Research, and Source Evaluation.
entries.text: chrome lesson 4 chrome lesson 4 accessible google chrome lesson 4: web search, research, and source evaluation. chrome lesson 4 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 4 web search, research, and source evaluation chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal search efficiently and record trustworthy workplace information. step-by-step instructions press ctrl+l and type a specific research question. review search results by heading with h and by link with tab or insert+f7. open one promising result in a new tab with ctrl+enter from the address bar suggestion or the available link context command. check the page title, organization, publication or update date, and web address. prefer official government, educational, manufacturer, or primary-source pages for factual instructions. compare the same fact with a second reliable source. do not enter personal information into an unfamiliar search form. record the question, two sources, dates, and the fact verified. return to the original tab and close unused tabs. save the research report as chrome-lesson-4.txt. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-4.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting the research question is specific. two sources and their organizations are recorded. the report explains why the sources are trustworthy. the file is chrome-lesson-4.txt. chrome manual next lesson chrome lesson 4.html

entries.title: Chrome Lesson 5
entries.snippet: Accessible Google Chrome Lesson 5: Bookmarks, History, and Finding a Page Again.
entries.text: chrome lesson 5 chrome lesson 5 accessible google chrome lesson 5: bookmarks, history, and finding a page again. chrome lesson 5 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 5 bookmarks, history, and finding a page again chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal save useful pages and recover previously visited information. step-by-step instructions open a safe page that will be useful later. press ctrl+d to open the bookmark dialog. give the bookmark a clear name and save it in an appropriate folder. press ctrl+shift+b to show or hide the bookmarks bar and observe how focus changes. press ctrl+shift+o to open bookmark manager. use ctrl+f within bookmark manager to find the saved bookmark. press ctrl+h to open history. search history for the practice page and open the correct result. remove only the practice bookmark if instructed; do not clear shared browsing history. write the difference between bookmarks and history in chrome-lesson-5.txt. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-5.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting bookmark creation and retrieval are documented. bookmarks and history are distinguished. the report warns against clearing shared data. the file is chrome-lesson-5.txt. chrome manual next lesson chrome lesson 5.html

entries.title: Chrome Lesson 6
entries.snippet: Accessible Google Chrome Lesson 6: Downloads, Uploads, and File Verification.
entries.text: chrome lesson 6 chrome lesson 6 accessible google chrome lesson 6: downloads, uploads, and file verification. chrome lesson 6 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 6 downloads, uploads, and file verification chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal download and upload files while confirming names, types, and locations. step-by-step instructions use only a trusted practice page offering a harmless file. before downloading, confirm the link text, source website, and expected file type. activate the download and press ctrl+j to open downloads. review the file name and status. use show in folder when available. in file explorer, verify the extension and use alt+enter to review properties. do not open a file if the name or type differs from what was expected. return to a lesson submission page in chrome. activate choose file, select a non-sensitive practice document, and confirm the selected file name before submitting. cancel the upload if the wrong file is selected; never upload client or confidential information. create chrome-lesson-6.txt with the download-and-upload safety checklist. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-6.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting source, file name, extension, and location checks are included. the report explains how to cancel a wrong selection. confidential-information protection is addressed. the file is chrome-lesson-6.txt. chrome manual next lesson chrome lesson 6.html

entries.title: Chrome Lesson 7
entries.snippet: Accessible Google Chrome Lesson 7: Forms, Forms Mode, and Site Permissions.
entries.text: chrome lesson 7 chrome lesson 7 accessible google chrome lesson 7: forms, forms mode, and site permissions. chrome lesson 7 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 7 forms, forms mode, and site permissions chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal complete browser forms and make careful decisions about site permission requests. step-by-step instructions open a safe practice form and keep the jaws virtual cursor on. press f or insert+f5 to locate form fields. press enter on an edit field to enter forms mode. use tab, shift+tab, spacebar, arrow keys, and alt+down arrow as appropriate for controls. use fictional practice information only. exit forms mode with num pad plus in the jaws desktop layout. when chrome requests notification, camera, microphone, or location permission, read the site name and requested permission before deciding. deny unexpected permission requests and ask authorized support before changing managed workplace permissions. review all form entries without submitting personal information. save a forms-and-permissions report as chrome-lesson-7.txt. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-7.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting forms mode and virtual cursor navigation are distinguished. at least four control types are described. permission requests are evaluated by site and purpose. the file is chrome-lesson-7.txt. chrome manual next lesson chrome lesson 7.html

entries.title: Chrome Lesson 8
entries.snippet: Accessible Google Chrome Lesson 8: Zoom, Full Screen, and Accessible Browser Settings.
entries.text: chrome lesson 8 chrome lesson 8 accessible google chrome lesson 8: zoom, full screen, and accessible browser settings. chrome lesson 8 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 8 zoom, full screen, and accessible browser settings chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal use chrome display and accessibility controls without disrupting screen-reader access. step-by-step instructions press ctrl+plus to increase page zoom and ctrl+minus to decrease it. press ctrl+0 to reset page zoom. press f11 to enter or leave full screen and note how browser controls change. open chrome settings with alt+f, then settings, or enter chrome://settings in the address bar. search settings for appearance and review font size and page zoom without changing shared settings. search for accessibility and review available options. test whether the page remains usable at 200 percent zoom. with jaws, verify headings, links, and form controls still work after zoom changes. return zoom to the learner’s preferred level. create chrome-lesson-8.txt describing useful adjustments and the difference between chrome settings and assistive-technology settings. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-8.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting zoom in, out, and reset commands are included. the page is evaluated at 200 percent. browser settings and screen-reader settings are distinguished. the file is chrome-lesson-8.txt. chrome manual next lesson chrome lesson 8.html

entries.title: Chrome Lesson 9
entries.snippet: Accessible Google Chrome Lesson 9: Privacy, Safe Browsing, Pop-ups, and Notifications.
entries.text: chrome lesson 9 chrome lesson 9 accessible google chrome lesson 9: privacy, safe browsing, pop-ups, and notifications. chrome lesson 9 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 9 privacy, safe browsing, pop-ups, and notifications chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal recognize browser warnings and manage privacy choices safely. step-by-step instructions open chrome settings and review privacy and security. review safety check without disabling protections. review safe browsing and do not select no protection. review site settings for notifications, pop-ups, camera, microphone, and location. remove or block only a clearly identified unwanted practice permission. do not bypass a deceptive-site or dangerous-download warning. use ctrl+shift+delete only to review the delete browsing data dialog, then cancel without clearing shared data. explain that incognito limits local history but does not make activity invisible to websites, employers, schools, or internet providers. close settings and confirm normal browsing still works. write a privacy-and-security checklist in chrome-lesson-9.txt. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-9.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting safe browsing remains enabled. at least four site permissions are covered. incognito limitations are explained. the file is chrome-lesson-9.txt. chrome manual next lesson chrome lesson 9.html

entries.title: Google Chrome Manual
entries.snippet: Accessible keyboard-first Google Chrome manual for Windows and JAWS users.
entries.text: google chrome manual google chrome manual accessible keyboard-first google chrome manual for windows and jaws users. google chrome manual - accessible learning center keyboard-first web browser manual google chrome manual practical chrome navigation, research, accessibility, downloads, forms, privacy, and safety. controls tabs jaws files privacy lessons address bar and browser controls ctrl+l: address bar. alt+left arrow and alt+right arrow: back and forward. ctrl+r: reload. esc: stop loading or dismiss a control. f6: cycle through the webpage and browser areas. ctrl+f: find text on the current page. ctrl+plus, ctrl+minus, ctrl+0: zoom in, out, and reset. tabs and windows ctrl+t: new tab. ctrl+tab and ctrl+shift+tab: next and previous tab. ctrl+1 through ctrl+8: numbered tab; ctrl+9: last tab. ctrl+w: close active tab. ctrl+shift+t: reopen last closed tab. ctrl+n: new window. alt+tab: switch applications or windows. confirm the active tab or window before closing it. chrome with jaws jaws normally uses the virtual cursor on webpages. h moves by heading, p by paragraph, l by list, i by list item, t by table, and f by form field. insert+f6 opens headings, insert+f7 links, and insert+f5 form fields. insert+ctrl+f performs jaws find; ctrl+f performs chrome find. press enter on a field to use forms mode and num pad plus to leave it in the jaws desktop layout. search and reliable research use specific search terms. check the organization, author or publisher, date, web address, and purpose. prefer primary and authoritative sources for factual instructions, and confirm important facts with a second reliable source. bookmarks, history, and downloads ctrl+d: bookmark current page. ctrl+shift+o: bookmark manager. ctrl+h: history. ctrl+j: downloads. verify a download’s source, filename, extension, and location before opening it. do not clear shared history or browsing data without permission. uploads and forms before uploading, confirm the selected filename and ensure it contains no private client or workplace information. on forms, read labels and required-field messages. review permission requests for notifications, camera, microphone, and location based on the site and task. accessibility and zoom chrome zoom changes webpage size; windows and assistive-technology settings affect the wider system. test pages at 200 percent zoom and ensure headings, links, controls, and content remain usable. website controls complement native browser, screen-reader, and device settings. privacy and safe browsing keep safe browsing enabled. do not bypass deceptive-site or dangerous-download warnings. grant site permissions only when the trusted site needs them for the current task. incognito limits local history but does not hide activity from websites, employers, schools, or internet providers. managed workplace settings may require administrator approval. official google references chrome keyboard shortcuts manage tabs in chrome manage warnings about unsafe sites chrome notification settings pop-ups and redirects google chrome lessons lesson 1: chrome layout, address bar, and basic navigation lesson 2: tabs, windows, and restoring work lesson 3: jaws web navigation in chrome lesson 4: web search, research, and source evaluation lesson 5: bookmarks, history, and finding a page again lesson 6: downloads, uploads, and file verification lesson 7: forms, forms mode, and site permissions lesson 8: zoom, full screen, and accessible browser settings lesson 9: privacy, safe browsing, pop-ups, and notifications lesson 10: final accessible workplace research project start chrome lesson 1 all chrome lessons my progress chrome manual.html

entries.title: Microsoft Copilot Manual
entries.snippet: Accessible keyboard-first Microsoft Copilot manual for blind and low-vision learners.
entries.text: microsoft copilot manual microsoft copilot manual accessible keyboard-first microsoft copilot manual for blind and low-vision learners. microsoft copilot manual - accessible learning center accessible microsoft copilot course microsoft copilot manual practical, responsible ai skills for work, learning, and independent problem-solving. basics prompting verification privacy screen readers lessons what generative ai does generative ai predicts and creates text or other content from patterns in training data and the information supplied in a conversation. it can help brainstorm, organize, explain, summarize, and draft. it does not understand a situation the way a person does, and it can produce confident but incorrect or invented information. use ai as an assistant, not as the final decision-maker. a person remains responsible for checking accuracy, appropriateness, accessibility, and compliance with workplace rules. a reliable prompt pattern task: state exactly what you want. context: explain the audience and purpose using nonprivate information. constraints: give length, tone, reading level, deadline, or other limits. format: request headings, bullets, a numbered procedure, or a simple table. checks: ask the tool to identify uncertainty and provide sources when appropriate. continue the conversation with specific follow-ups. for example: “shorten this to 150 words,” “explain the second step,” or “which statements need verification?” verify before using the result open original sources instead of trusting an ai summary or citation. confirm names, dates, quotations, calculations, contact details, laws, policies, and software instructions. prefer current primary sources from the organization responsible for the information. compare important claims with a second reliable source. test instructions safely before giving them to another person. rewrite the final result in your own voice and keep a record of corrections. privacy and workplace rules do not enter client records, medical or disability details, passwords, financial account information, private addresses, confidential workplace material, copyrighted documents you are not permitted to share, or information that identifies another person. use fictional or public information in these lessons. follow the employer’s approved-tool, retention, disclosure, and human-review requirements. a personal free account is not automatically approved for organizational data. never allow ai to make an employment, benefit, medical, legal, financial, safety, or accommodation decision for a person. accessible output ask for descriptive headings, short paragraphs, meaningful link text, numbered steps, and simple tables. ask for image descriptions when an image matters, but verify the description with a trusted person when accuracy is important. avoid layouts that communicate meaning only through color, position, or visual formatting. jaws, narrator, and nvda ai interfaces change often. use tab and shift+tab to move among controls, enter or space to activate a control, and the screen reader’s heading, landmark, link, button, edit-field, and browse-mode commands to review the page. use browser find to locate words such as “sources,” “copy,” or part of your prompt. jaws: h moves by heading, b by button, e by edit field, insert+f7 opens links, and insert+f5 opens form fields. nvda: h moves by heading, b by button, e by edit field, nvda+f7 opens the elements list, and nvda+space switches browse and focus modes. narrator: use caps lock or insert with arrow keys for scan mode navigation; press caps lock+space to toggle scan mode when needed. after sending a prompt, allow time for the response to finish. move by heading or paragraph and confirm whether focus changed. product-specific keyboard behavior may change after updates. free-course rule these lessons can be completed with an available free ai service or by studying the examples without creating an account. do not start a paid trial, enter payment information, or purchase a subscription for this course. official references official microsoft copilot help and learning microsoft copilot on windows microsoft copilot lessons lesson 1: open copilot and understand its main controls lesson 2: write clear prompts for microsoft work tasks lesson 3: refine responses with follow-up instructions lesson 4: draft and improve professional messages lesson 5: summarize public documents and verify key points lesson 6: create word, excel, and powerpoint planning content lesson 7: research with citations and check original sources lesson 8: protect organizational data and follow permissions lesson 9: use copilot with jaws, narrator, or nvda lesson 10: final microsoft copilot workplace project start entries.text: nls braille ereader manual nls braille ereader accessible manual accessible nls braille ereader manual for keyboard and jaws users. nls braille ereader manual - accessible learning center accessible technology manual nls braille ereader accessible manual a keyboard-first guide for blind and low-vision learners using jaws. all manuals ten nls braille ereader lessons my progress purpose and setup this manual supports independent practice with nls braille ereader on windows. use the exact software version, device model, account permissions, and workplace policy available to you. commands and labels can change after updates. start jaws before opening the application or connecting a braille device. use insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focus, and insert+1 for keyboard help. practice with fictional, public, instructor-provided, or redacted information only. never submit passwords, recovery codes, government identifiers, protected books, or private workplace data. save a backup before changing, deleting, converting, or remediating a file. ten-lesson learning path lesson 1: orientation, power, and main menu — create a tactile orientation and power checklist. lesson 2: bookshelf and file organization — submit a bookshelf navigation log. lesson 3: read and navigate a book — create a reading-navigation command reference. lesson 4: search, bookmarks, and reading position — submit a search-and-bookmark report. lesson 5: notes and the editor — create nls-ereader-lesson-5.txt or brf. lesson 6: obtain and transfer nls bard content — write a credential-free bard transfer checklist. lesson 7: terminal mode and computer connection — submit a terminal-mode connection log or a model-capability report. lesson 8: settings, language, and status — create a settings inventory without serial numbers. lesson 9: safe troubleshooting and updates — create a safe troubleshooting decision guide. lesson 10: final independent reading project — complete an independent accessible-reading workflow. accessible working routine confirm the window, document, device, or webpage title. identify keyboard focus before typing or activating a control. navigate by real structure—headings, lists, fields, tables, or menus—when available. review the result with jaws or a braille display from beginning to end. verify the destination and filename before saving, uploading, sharing, or deleting. use the course’s private assignment uploader only for the requested practice file. important: these course controls complement, and do not replace, browser, operating-system, screen-reader, braille-display, or other assistive-technology settings. official references use these primary sources when a label or command differs from the lesson: nls braille ereader resources nls humanware ereader user guide start nls braille ereader lesson 1 return to manuals ereader manual.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 1
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 1: Excel Basics: Workbooks, Worksheets, and Cells.
entries.text: excel lesson 1 excel lesson 1 accessible microsoft excel lesson 1: excel basics: workbooks, worksheets, and cells. excel lesson 1 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 1 excel basics: workbooks, worksheets, and cells excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal open excel, understand the worksheet grid, enter a simple workplace contact list, and save a workbook. skills practiced identify a workbook, worksheet, row, column, cell, and cell address. move one cell at a time with the arrow keys. enter and correct text in cells. save an excel workbook as an xlsx file. step-by-step instructions open microsoft excel and create a blank workbook. jaws announces the active cell address and its contents. the first cell is a1. type name in a1, press tab, type department in b1, press tab, and type extension in c1. press home to return to column a in the current row. in row 2, enter jordan lee, training, and 4101. use tab after each entry. in row 3, enter morgan reed, technology, and 4102. in row 4, enter casey hall, employment, and 4103. use the arrow keys to review each cell. press insert+up arrow to hear the current line or cell information when useful. press ctrl+s. choose a folder you can locate later. save the workbook as excel-lesson-1.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create a three-column employee contact list with the headers name, department, and extension. include at least five fictional employees. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-1.xlsx . before submitting row 1 contains clear column headers. at least five fictional employee records are included. there are no completely blank rows inside the list. the file is saved as excel-lesson-1.xlsx. excel manual next lesson excel lesson 1.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 10
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 10: Final Employment Workbook Project.
entries.text: excel lesson 10 excel lesson 10 accessible microsoft excel lesson 10: final employment workbook project. excel lesson 10 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 10 final employment workbook project excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal independently build an accessible workbook that organizes, calculates, summarizes, and communicates workplace information. skills practiced plan an accessible table structure. use formulas and functions accurately. organize multiple worksheets. create an accessible summary for a supervisor. step-by-step instructions create a workbook for a fictional department's monthly supply budget. create a purchases worksheet with the headers date, item, category, quantity, unit cost, and line total. enter at least ten fictional purchases across at least three categories. use a formula to calculate each line total. format dates and currency appropriately without merging cells. convert the purchase list to a table and give it a meaningful name. create a summary worksheet. calculate the grand total, average line total, lowest line total, and highest line total. use countif to count at least one category or status. create one simple chart from summary data, add meaningful alt text, and keep its source data available. add a plain-text summary that explains the most important result. run the accessibility checker and review every worksheet using only the keyboard. save the workbook as excel-lesson-10-final.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment complete an accessible monthly supply-budget workbook with at least ten purchases, formulas, a table, summary calculations, a chart with alt text, and a written summary. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-10-final.xlsx . before submitting the purchases worksheet contains at least ten complete records. all line totals and summary calculations use formulas. the workbook includes a clearly named summary worksheet. the chart has alt text and its source data remains available. there are no merged cells or color-only instructions. the accessibility checker was reviewed. the file is saved as excel-lesson-10-final.xlsx. previous lesson view course progress excel lesson 10.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 2
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 2: Navigating, Editing, Finding, and Filling Data.
entries.text: excel lesson 2 excel lesson 2 accessible microsoft excel lesson 2: navigating, editing, finding, and filling data. excel lesson 2 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 2 navigating, editing, finding, and filling data excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal move efficiently through a worksheet, edit cells, find and replace information, and copy values without relying on a mouse. skills practiced move to data boundaries with ctrl+arrow. use ctrl+g to go directly to a cell. edit a cell with f2. use find and replace. copy and paste a value or formula. step-by-step instructions open excel-lesson-1.xlsx. press ctrl+home to move to a1. press ctrl+end to move to the last used cell. press ctrl+g, type b3, and press enter to move directly to cell b3. press f2, change the department in b3 to customer service, and press enter. press ctrl+f, type employment, and press enter to locate that word. press escape to close find. press ctrl+h. replace training with learning services, then close the dialog. add a fourth column header in d1 named status. type active in d2. copy d2 with ctrl+c, select d3 through the last employee row with shift+down arrow, and press ctrl+v. review the list with ctrl+arrow and arrow keys. press f12 or use file, save as, and save a copy as excel-lesson-2.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment update the contact list so one department is customer service, training is replaced with learning services, and every employee has active in the status column. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-2.xlsx . before submitting the original headers remain present. customer service and learning services appear in the department column. every employee row has active in the status column. the file is saved as excel-lesson-2.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 2.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 3
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 3: Formulas, AutoSum, and Basic Calculations.
entries.text: excel lesson 3 excel lesson 3 accessible microsoft excel lesson 3: formulas, autosum, and basic calculations. excel lesson 3 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 3 formulas, autosum, and basic calculations excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal create a small expense worksheet and calculate totals and averages with formulas. skills practiced enter formulas beginning with an equals sign. use cell references in calculations. use autosum with alt+equals. use sum, average, min, and max. step-by-step instructions create a blank workbook. in a1 through c1, enter item, quantity, and unit cost. enter five fictional office supply items in rows 2 through 6 with quantities and unit costs. in d1, enter line total. in d2, type =b2*c2 and press enter. copy d2 and paste it into d3 through d6. excel adjusts the row references. in c8, enter grand total. in d8, press alt+equals, confirm the range d2:d6, and press enter. in c9, enter average cost. in d9, type =average(d2:d6) and press enter. in c10, enter lowest cost. in d10, type =min(d2:d6). in c11, enter highest cost. in d11, type =max(d2:d6). use f2 on each result cell to review the formula, then press escape without changing it. save the workbook as excel-lesson-3.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create an office-supply expense worksheet with at least five items, line totals, a grand total, an average, a minimum, and a maximum. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-3.xlsx . before submitting all formulas begin with an equals sign. line totals use quantity multiplied by unit cost. summary formulas reference the correct range. the file is saved as excel-lesson-3.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 3.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 4
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 4: Accessible Formatting and Number Formats.
entries.text: excel lesson 4 excel lesson 4 accessible microsoft excel lesson 4: accessible formatting and number formats. excel lesson 4 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 4 accessible formatting and number formats excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal apply meaningful formatting and number formats while keeping the worksheet usable with screen readers and magnification. skills practiced open format cells with ctrl+1. apply currency, percentage, date, and text formats. use bold and clear headers. avoid merged cells and color-only meaning. step-by-step instructions open excel-lesson-3.xlsx. select the header row from a1 through d1 and press ctrl+b. select the unit cost and line total values. press ctrl+1 to open format cells. choose currency or accounting with two decimal places, then press enter. add a discount column in e1. enter percentages such as 5%, 10%, and 0% in e2 through e6. use ctrl+1 to confirm the discount cells use percentage format. add a purchase date column in f1 and enter valid dates for each item. use ctrl+1 to apply a clear date format. do not merge cells. keep one header for every column and one record per row. if you use color, also include text such as approved or review so color is not the only cue. run review, check accessibility by pressing alt+q, typing check accessibility, and choosing the command. save the workbook as excel-lesson-4.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment format the expense worksheet with bold headers, currency, percentage, and date formats. keep the structure accessible and do not merge cells. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-4.xlsx . before submitting headers are bold and descriptive. money, percentages, and dates use appropriate number formats. no cells are merged. color is not the only way information is communicated. the file is saved as excel-lesson-4.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 4.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 5
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 5: Tables, Sorting, and Filtering.
entries.text: excel lesson 5 excel lesson 5 accessible microsoft excel lesson 5: tables, sorting, and filtering. excel lesson 5 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 5 tables, sorting, and filtering excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal convert data into an accessible excel table and use keyboard commands to sort and filter records. skills practiced create a table with ctrl+t. confirm that the table has headers. open a column filter with alt+down arrow. sort and filter workplace data. step-by-step instructions create a blank workbook with the headers employee, department, training status, and due date in row 1. enter at least eight fictional employee records. use complete, in progress, or not started in the training status column. select any cell in the list and press ctrl+t. confirm the correct range and check my table has headers, then press enter. move to a header cell and press alt+down arrow to open its filter menu. in the department header, sort a to z using the menu. in the training status header, filter the table so only not started records remain. review the visible rows with the arrow keys. open the filter again and choose clear filter so all records return. give the table a meaningful name through table design if available, such as trainingtracker. save the workbook as excel-lesson-5.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create a training tracker with at least eight fictional employees, convert it to a table, sort by department, and confirm that filtering by training status works. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-5.xlsx . before submitting the list is formatted as an excel table. the table includes unique, descriptive headers. at least eight records are included. there are no blank rows or columns inside the table. the file is saved as excel-lesson-5.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 5.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 6
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 6: IF, COUNTIF, and Conditional Results.
entries.text: excel lesson 6 excel lesson 6 accessible microsoft excel lesson 6: if, countif, and conditional results. excel lesson 6 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 6 if, countif, and conditional results excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal use logical and counting functions to turn raw workplace data into useful status information. skills practiced use if to return one of two text results. use countif to count records that meet a condition. copy formulas down a column. check formula ranges and quotation marks. step-by-step instructions create a workbook with the headers employee, completed hours, required hours, and status. enter six fictional employees. give each person completed hours and a required-hours goal. in d2, type =if(b2>=c2,"complete","needs training") and press enter. copy the formula from d2 through all employee rows. below the list, enter complete count in c10. in d10, type =countif(d2:d7,"complete") and press enter. adjust the ending row if your list is longer. enter needs training count in c11. in d11, type =countif(d2:d7,"needs training") and press enter. use f2 to inspect a copied if formula and confirm its row references changed. use ctrl+grave accent to show formulas if available, then press it again to return to results. save the workbook as excel-lesson-6.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create a six-person training-hours tracker that automatically labels each person complete or needs training and counts both results. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-6.xlsx . before submitting the if formula compares completed hours with required hours. every employee row contains a status formula. countif totals both status categories. the file is saved as excel-lesson-6.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 6.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 7
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 7: Managing Worksheets and Cross-Sheet References.
entries.text: excel lesson 7 excel lesson 7 accessible microsoft excel lesson 7: managing worksheets and cross-sheet references. excel lesson 7 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 7 managing worksheets and cross-sheet references excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal organize related information across worksheets and create a summary that refers to another sheet. skills practiced insert a worksheet with shift+f11. move between sheets with ctrl+page up and ctrl+page down. rename worksheets. reference a cell on another worksheet. step-by-step instructions create a blank workbook and rename sheet1 to january. use alt+q and search for rename sheet if ribbon keytips differ. enter category and amount in a1 and b1. enter five fictional january expenses in rows 2 through 6. press shift+f11 to insert a new worksheet and rename it february. enter the same headers and five fictional february expenses. press shift+f11 again and rename the new worksheet summary. use ctrl+page up and ctrl+page down to move among the three worksheets. on january, calculate the total in b8 with =sum(b2:b6). do the same on february. on summary, enter january total in a1 and type =january!b8 in b1. enter february total in a2 and type =february!b8 in b2. enter combined total in a3 and type =sum(b1:b2) in b3. save the workbook as excel-lesson-7.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create january, february, and summary worksheets. enter expenses on the monthly sheets and show both monthly totals plus a combined total on summary. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-7.xlsx . before submitting all three worksheets have meaningful names. monthly totals use sum formulas. summary references the monthly worksheets. ctrl+page up and ctrl+page down move among the sheets. the file is saved as excel-lesson-7.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 7.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 8
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 8: Charts, Alternative Text, and Accessibility Checker.
entries.text: excel lesson 8 excel lesson 8 accessible microsoft excel lesson 8: charts, alternative text, and accessibility checker. excel lesson 8 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 8 charts, alternative text, and accessibility checker excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal create a simple chart, provide a text equivalent, and use excel accessibility checks. skills practiced create a chart from a small data table. add meaningful alternative text. provide the same key information in worksheet cells. run the accessibility checker. step-by-step instructions create a two-column table with month and completed trainings. enter january through june and fictional completion totals. select the table, including headers. press alt+f1 to create a chart on the current worksheet. use f6 to move focus among the worksheet, ribbon, and chart objects until jaws announces the chart. open the chart context menu with shift+f10. use format chart area or alt text options to add a description. write concise alt text that explains the chart's purpose and important trend, not every visual detail. keep the source data table in the workbook so screen-reader users can inspect exact values. add a cell below the table containing a short text summary of the trend. press alt+q, type check accessibility, and run the accessibility checker. review and resolve issues that apply. do not remove the source table. save the workbook as excel-lesson-8.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create a six-month training-completion chart, add meaningful alternative text, retain the source data, and include a plain-text trend summary. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-8.xlsx . before submitting the chart is based on a clearly labeled data table. the chart has useful alternative text. a text summary identifies the main trend. the accessibility checker was reviewed. the file is saved as excel-lesson-8.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 8.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 9
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 9: Data Validation, Consistent Entry, and Review.
entries.text: excel lesson 9 excel lesson 9 accessible microsoft excel lesson 9: data validation, consistent entry, and review. excel lesson 9 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 9 data validation, consistent entry, and review excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal create a reliable data-entry sheet with controlled choices and check it for common accessibility problems. skills practiced create a drop-down list with data validation. use consistent data types. find blanks and errors. document instructions inside the workbook. step-by-step instructions create a blank workbook with the headers request id, request type, priority, assigned to, and status. enter five fictional requests. in a separate area, list the allowed status values: new, in progress, waiting, and closed. select the status entry cells. press alt+q, type data validation, and choose the command. choose list and set the source to the cells containing the allowed status values. use alt+down arrow in a validated status cell to open its choices, then select a value. apply a similar list to priority using low, medium, and high. add an instructions worksheet explaining what each column contains and which values are allowed. use ctrl+f to search for blank required fields and review the used range with ctrl+end. run check accessibility and correct merged cells, unclear sheet names, or missing object descriptions. save the workbook as excel-lesson-9.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create a small service-request tracker with validated status and priority choices plus an instructions worksheet. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-9.xlsx . before submitting status and priority use controlled lists. every request has a unique request id. the instructions worksheet explains the fields. no required cells are blank. the file is saved as excel-lesson-9.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 9.html

entries.title: Microsoft Excel Accessible Manual
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel manual for Microsoft 365 desktop on Windows with JAWS and keyboard-first instruction.
entries.text: microsoft excel manual microsoft excel accessible manual accessible microsoft excel manual for microsoft 365 desktop on windows with jaws and keyboard-first instruction. microsoft excel manual - accessible learning center keyboard-first microsoft 365 training microsoft excel accessible manual a practical guide to creating, navigating, calculating, organizing, and checking spreadsheets with jaws on windows. keyboard quick reference accessible workbook practices course lessons about this manual this manual is written for microsoft excel in microsoft 365 desktop on windows. it focuses on keyboard use with jaws, but most standard excel shortcuts also work with other screen readers and magnification. excel is organized as workbooks containing worksheets. each worksheet is a grid of columns, rows, and cells. a cell address combines its column letter and row number, such as b4. jaws normally announces the active cell address, cell contents, and useful formatting or formula information. microsoft 365 changes over time. if a ribbon keytip differs, press alt+q , type the command name, and choose it from search. for jaws command help, press insert+spacebar, then j to open jaws commands search. keyboard quick reference common excel and jaws commands used in this course task command move one cell arrow keys move to the edge of a data region ctrl+arrow key move to cell a1 ctrl+home move to the last used cell ctrl+end go directly to a cell ctrl+g, type the cell address, enter edit the active cell f2 find or replace ctrl+f or ctrl+h save ctrl+s save as f12 open format cells ctrl+1 autosum alt+equals create a table ctrl+t open a table header filter alt+down arrow move to next or previous worksheet ctrl+page down or ctrl+page up insert a worksheet shift+f11 create a chart on the current sheet alt+f1 office command search alt+q jaws commands search insert+spacebar, then j list cells with data in current column insert+shift+c list cells with data in current row insert+shift+r accessible workbook practices use a short, unique header for every column and keep headers in one row. keep one kind of information in each column and one record in each row. avoid merged cells. screen readers can repeat, skip, or misidentify merged content. avoid blank rows and columns inside a data table. use real number formats for currency, percentages, and dates instead of typing visual symbols as text. do not use color as the only way to communicate status or instructions. include words or symbols with text equivalents. give worksheets meaningful names and remove unused blank worksheets before sharing. for charts and other visual objects, add concise alternative text and keep the source data available in cells. use an excel table when possible so headers and data boundaries are explicit. run review, check accessibility before submitting or sharing a workbook. formula essentials every excel formula begins with an equals sign. a formula can contain numbers, cell references, operators, and functions. =b2*c2 multiplies the values in b2 and c2. =sum(d2:d10) adds the values from d2 through d10. =average(d2:d10) calculates the average. =min(d2:d10) and =max(d2:d10) return the lowest and highest values. =if(b2>=c2,"complete","needs training") returns text based on a condition. =countif(d2:d10,"complete") counts cells matching the word complete. press f2 to edit and inspect the active cell's formula. when copying formulas, confirm that relative cell references changed as intended. tables, sorting, and filtering select a cell in a continuous data list and press ctrl+t to create a table. confirm the range and that the table has headers. on a table header, press alt+down arrow to open sorting and filtering choices. after filtering, remember that some rows are hidden. clear filters before sharing unless the filtered view is intentional, and describe the active filter in a nearby cell or instructions worksheet. charts and nonvisual access a chart should never be the only source of information. keep the labeled source table, add useful alternative text, and include a short text summary of the important trend or conclusion. avoid descriptions such as “chart” that do not explain its purpose. ten-lesson course sequence lesson 1: excel basics: workbooks, worksheets, and cells — open excel, understand the worksheet grid, enter a simple workplace contact list, and save a workbook. lesson 2: navigating, editing, finding, and filling data — move efficiently through a worksheet, edit cells, find and replace information, and copy values without relying on a mouse. lesson 3: formulas, autosum, and basic calculations — create a small expense worksheet and calculate totals and averages with formulas. lesson 4: accessible formatting and number formats — apply meaningful formatting and number formats while keeping the worksheet usable with screen readers and magnification. lesson 5: tables, sorting, and filtering — convert data into an accessible excel table and use keyboard commands to sort and filter records. lesson 6: if, countif, and conditional results — use logical and counting functions to turn raw workplace data into useful status information. lesson 7: managing worksheets and cross-sheet references — organize related information across worksheets and create a summary that refers to another sheet. lesson 8: charts, alternative text, and accessibility checker — create a simple chart, provide a text equivalent, and use excel accessibility checks. lesson 9: data validation, consistent entry, and review — create a reliable data-entry sheet with controlled choices and check it for common accessibility problems. lesson 10: final employment workbook project — independently build an accessible workbook that organizes, calculates, summarizes, and communicates workplace information. begin excel lesson 1 official references and further learning microsoft: accessibility best practices with excel spreadsheets microsoft: screen reader support for excel microsoft: accessibility checker freedom scientific: excel productivity with jaws freedom scientific: navigating excel spreadsheets with jaws view excel lessons view my progress return to manuals excel manual.html

identify your focus model first this course emphasizes the focus 40 blue fifth generation. a fifth-generation focus has a menu button centered between braille keys 1 and 4. older focus 40 blue models have different controls, ports, features, and firmware. never install firmware until the exact model and generation are confirmed. use the official guide for the assigned device generation. start jaws before connecting the focus to windows. save open work before changing connections or settings. use instructor-provided or fictional files during practice. never submit passwords, pairing codes, serial numbers, protected books, or private workplace information. major controls and features 40 refreshable braille cells: display one line of computer text in braille. cursor router buttons: move the cursor, activate links, and support text selection. perkins-style keyboard and braillein: enter text and windows or jaws commands. panning buttons, rocker bars, and nav rockers: move through text and structured information. usb and bluetooth: connect to computers and supported mobile devices. fifth-generation scratchpad and brf book reader: create notes and read supported files without a computer. ten-lesson learning path lesson 1: orientation, power, and device identification — create a tactile orientation guide naming the major controls and explaining how to identify the device generation. lesson 2: connect by usb and configure jaws — write a usb connection and jaws verification checklist. lesson 3: pair and manage bluetooth connections — create a credential-free bluetooth pairing and connection-switching guide. lesson 4: read, pan, route the cursor, and select text — submit a command chart for panning, navigation, cursor routing, and text selection. lesson 5: type with braillein and edit text — create focus-lesson-5.txt or docx containing a short corrected workplace note. lesson 6: navigate windows, file explorer, and documents — create a keyboard-and-braille workflow for finding and reading a workplace file. lesson 7: navigate webpages, forms, lists, and tables — document an accessible web-navigation practice session. lesson 8: use scratchpad, brf book reader, and microsd safely — create a local note and a storage-safety checklist; submit only your original note. lesson 9: braille settings, study mode, cleaning, and updates — create a safe settings, cleaning, and firmware checklist. lesson 10: final focus 40 blue workplace project — complete an end-to-end focus 40 blue workplace task and submit only the original summary. safe working routine identify the focus model and generation. confirm power, battery, cable, and connection mode. confirm the active jaws braille display and windows focus. practice on a copy and verify the destination before saving or transferring. restore reversible settings after practice. disconnect, clean, and update only according to the official instructions. official freedom scientific references focus blue fifth-generation user guide focus blue training and jaws features focus 40 blue documentation focus blue quick-start guide start focus 40 blue lesson 1 return to manuals focus manual.html

entries.title: Choosing a Free Office Suite Manual
entries.snippet: Accessible keyboard-first Choosing a Free Office Suite manual for blind and low-vision learners.
entries.text: choosing a free office suite manual choosing a free office suite manual accessible keyboard-first choosing a free office suite manual for blind and low-vision learners. choosing a free office suite manual - accessible learning center free office software foundations choosing a free office suite manual no-cost office skills, accessible workflows, and microsoft-compatible file exchange. cost accessibility file formats screen readers compatibility lessons no-cost course rule this course must not require a purchase, subscription, paid trial, payment card, or new paid service. libreoffice is free and open source. google docs editors and microsoft 365 for the web have free account-based options, but internet access, account rules, storage limits, and available features can differ. use an employer-approved program and account for workplace information. a free personal account is not automatically approved for client or organizational data. accessibility comes before feature count before choosing a program, test the actual work tasks with the learner’s preferred screen reader, braille display, magnification, browser zoom, color settings, and keyboard. confirm that focus is announced, controls have useful names, editing feedback is understandable, and essential tasks do not require a mouse. use descriptive headings, real lists, clear table headers, meaningful links, alternative text, sufficient contrast, and logical reading order. do not communicate meaning only through color or visual position. run the program’s accessibility checker when available, but also perform a keyboard and screen-reader review. keep an original editable file before exporting pdf or converting formats. native and exchange formats libreoffice native formats odt for writer, ods for calc, and odp for impress preserve libreoffice editing features. microsoft exchange formats docx, xlsx, and pptx are often required by employers or instructors using microsoft 365. other formats csv carries plain spreadsheet data without formulas or formatting. pdf is useful for fixed-layout review but may be harder to edit and must be checked for accessibility. save the native version first. then save or download a separate exchange copy and review it in the receiving program whenever possible. jaws, narrator, and nvda interfaces vary by program and update. use tab and shift+tab for controls, arrow keys within menus and lists, enter or space to activate, alt or f10 for menus when supported, ctrl+s to save, ctrl+o to open, and ctrl+z to undo. listen for the current control name and state instead of memorizing screen position. jaws: use insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. nvda: use nvda+t for the title, nvda+tab for focus, and nvda+1 for input help. narrator: use caps lock+t for the title and caps lock+1 for input learning. toggle scan mode only when the application or webpage requires it. browser-based editors may have their own screen-reader-support setting and keyboard shortcuts. read the current official help before changing screen-reader modes. compatibility review keep an untouched native copy. create a separate docx, xlsx, pptx, csv, or pdf copy. read every heading, cell range, slide title, link, table, image description, formula result, note, and page or slide count. check fonts, spacing, page breaks, charts, animations, formulas, comments, and accessibility metadata. correct the native file and export again rather than repeatedly converting the same exchange copy. never promise perfect compatibility without testing the actual document in the receiving software. privacy, accounts, and sharing use fictional or public information in these lessons. do not upload client records, medical or disability information, passwords, financial data, or confidential workplace material. for cloud tools, confirm the active account and sharing permission before entering content. for local tools, back up files to an approved location. official references libreoffice suite overview microsoft 365 for the web google docs editors help choosing a free office suite
