entries.text: word lesson 1 microsoft word lesson 1  word lesson 1 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 1 opening word, creating, and saving a document goal learn how to open microsoft word, create a blank document, enter text, and save the document. instructions press the windows key. type word. press enter on microsoft word. press ctrl+n to create a blank document. type the heading: my first word document press enter twice. type: i am learning to use microsoft word independently with a screen reader. press enter twice. type: i can create, type, save, and reopen word documents. press ctrl+s. choose a location you can find again. name the file word-lesson-1. save it as a docx file. your assignment complete the assignment and save it as: word-lesson-1.docx before submitting make sure all required text is present. make sure the file is saved as docx. make sure the filename is word-lesson-1. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 1.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 10
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 10 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 10 Final Independent Word Assignment Goal Demonstrate the Microsoft Word skills you have practiced throughout Lessons 1 through 9. Your Assignment Create a one-page document
entries.text: word lesson 10 microsoft word lesson 10  word lesson 10 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 10 final independent word assignment goal demonstrate the microsoft word skills you have practiced throughout lessons 1 through 9. your assignment create a one-page document titled my accessible technology skills . requirements create the document independently. use the title my accessible technology skills. apply heading 1 to the title. create at least two heading 2 sections. write at least two paragraphs of body text. include one bulleted or numbered list containing at least three items. include one simple table containing at least three columns and three rows. make the first table row a header row. include one descriptive hyperlink. use at least one example of bold or italic formatting. run spelling and grammar review. run accessibility checker or accessibility assistant. correct important accessibility issues that word identifies. save the document as word-lesson-10-final.docx. create a pdf copy if you are able to do so. what the assignment checker will review document structure correct use of headings paragraph content lists table structure meaningful hyperlink text basic formatting accessibility filename overall organization remember the goal is not perfection. the goal is to demonstrate that you can create and organize a word document independently. feedback will identify what you did well and a small number of things to improve next time. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 10.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 2
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 2 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 2 Moving, Selecting, and Editing Text Goal Practice moving through text, selecting words, correcting mistakes, copying, cutting, pasting, undoing, and redoing. Instructions Op
entries.text: word lesson 2 microsoft word lesson 2  word lesson 2 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 2 moving, selecting, and editing text goal practice moving through text, selecting words, correcting mistakes, copying, cutting, pasting, undoing, and redoing. instructions open microsoft word and create a blank document. type: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. press enter twice. type: microsoft word makes document editing easy. use ctrl+left arrow and ctrl+right arrow to move by word. use left arrow and right arrow to move by character. select the word easy using ctrl+shift+left arrow or ctrl+shift+right arrow. replace easy with efficient. select the words microsoft word. press ctrl+c to copy them. move to the end of the document. press enter twice and press ctrl+v. press ctrl+z to undo the paste. press ctrl+y to redo it. save the file as word-lesson-2.docx. your assignment submit word-lesson-2.docx . before submitting the word easy should have been replaced with efficient. microsoft word should appear again at the bottom of the document. the file should be saved correctly. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 2.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 3
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 3 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 3 Find, Replace, Save, Close, and Reopen Goal Learn how to find text, replace text, save a document, close it, and reopen it. Instructions Create a new Word document. Type thr
entries.text: word lesson 3 microsoft word lesson 3  word lesson 3 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 3 find, replace, save, close, and reopen goal learn how to find text, replace text, save a document, close it, and reopen it. instructions create a new word document. type three short paragraphs containing the word computer at least four times. press ctrl+f. search for computer. move through the search results. close the navigation pane with escape. press ctrl+h. replace one occurrence of computer with technology. do not use replace all. save the file as word-lesson-3.docx. press ctrl+w to close the document. press ctrl+o. locate word-lesson-3.docx and reopen it. press ctrl+home and verify the document contents. your assignment submit word-lesson-3.docx . before submitting the document should contain three paragraphs. at least one occurrence of computer should be changed to technology. the document should have been successfully saved and reopened. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 3.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 4
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 4 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 4 Formatting Text and Paragraphs Goal Practice bold, italics, underline, alignment, and basic paragraph formatting. Instructions Create a blank Word document. Type the title:
entries.text: word lesson 4 microsoft word lesson 4  word lesson 4 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 4 formatting text and paragraphs goal practice bold, italics, underline, alignment, and basic paragraph formatting. instructions create a blank word document. type the title: accessible technology skills press enter twice. type: technology can increase independence at work, school, and home. press enter twice. type: learning keyboard commands can make common tasks faster. make the title bold. center the title using ctrl+e. make the words increase independence italic. underline the words keyboard commands. make sure both body paragraphs are left aligned using ctrl+l. save the document as word-lesson-4.docx. your assignment submit word-lesson-4.docx . before submitting the title should be bold and centered. the requested phrase should be italic. the requested phrase should be underlined. the body paragraphs should be left aligned. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 4.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 5
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 5 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 5 Headings, Styles, and Document Navigation Goal Learn to create a properly structured document using Word's built-in heading styles. Instructions Create a blank Word document
entries.text: word lesson 5 microsoft word lesson 5  word lesson 5 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 5 headings, styles, and document navigation goal learn to create a properly structured document using word's built-in heading styles. instructions create a blank word document. type: my technology training plan apply heading 1 using ctrl+alt+1. press enter and type: microsoft word apply heading 2 using ctrl+alt+2. press enter and apply normal style using ctrl+shift+n. type one sentence about learning microsoft word. press enter twice and type: internet skills apply heading 2. press enter and return to normal style. type one sentence about learning internet skills. press ctrl+f. move to the headings section of the navigation pane. verify that your headings appear. navigate between the headings. save as word-lesson-5.docx. your assignment submit word-lesson-5.docx . before submitting the main title should use heading 1. microsoft word should use heading 2. internet skills should use heading 2. body text should use normal style. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 5.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 6
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 6 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 6 Bulleted and Numbered Lists Goal Create structured bulleted and numbered lists that screen readers can recognize. Instructions Create a blank Word document. Type the heading
entries.text: word lesson 6 microsoft word lesson 6  word lesson 6 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 6 bulleted and numbered lists goal create structured bulleted and numbered lists that screen readers can recognize. instructions create a blank word document. type the heading: daily technology checklist apply heading 1. press enter and return to normal style. press ctrl+shift+l to begin a bulleted list. enter: check email enter: review calendar enter: complete assignments enter: save important files press enter twice to end the list. type the heading: steps for saving a document apply heading 2. create a numbered list containing: open the file menu, choose save as, choose a folder, enter a filename, and choose save. save the file as word-lesson-6.docx. your assignment submit word-lesson-6.docx . before submitting the document should contain one true bulleted list. the document should contain one true numbered list. headings should use built-in heading styles. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 6.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 7
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 7 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 7 Creating Accessible Tables Goal Learn to create and navigate a simple table with a header row. Instructions Create a blank Word document. Type the heading: Training Schedule
entries.text: word lesson 7 microsoft word lesson 7  word lesson 7 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 7 creating accessible tables goal learn to create and navigate a simple table with a header row. instructions create a blank word document. type the heading: training schedule apply heading 1. insert a table with 3 columns and 4 rows. use these column headings in the first row: topic, date, status. enter microsoft word, monday, complete in the second row. enter excel, tuesday, in progress in the third row. enter powerpoint, wednesday, not started in the fourth row. make the first row the table's header row. use tab and shift+tab to move through the cells. avoid merged or split cells. save the file as word-lesson-7.docx. your assignment submit word-lesson-7.docx . before submitting the table should contain 3 columns and 4 rows. the first row should contain topic, date, and status. the first row should be designated as a header row. the table should not contain merged cells. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 7.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 8
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 8 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 8 Links, Alt Text, and Accessibility Goal Practice creating meaningful links, working with images, and checking document accessibility. Instructions Create a blank Word docume
entries.text: word lesson 8 microsoft word lesson 8  word lesson 8 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 8 links, alt text, and accessibility goal practice creating meaningful links, working with images, and checking document accessibility. instructions create a blank word document. type the heading: accessible documents apply heading 1. type: accessible documents can be used effectively by people with disabilities. press enter twice. type the words microsoft accessibility. select those words. press ctrl+k. enter a microsoft accessibility web address. confirm that the visible link text remains microsoft accessibility instead of displaying only a raw url. if you are able to insert an image, add one practice image. add concise alt text describing the image's purpose. if the image is decorative, mark it decorative instead. open review and run accessibility checker or accessibility assistant. correct any accessibility problems you can identify. save as word-lesson-8.docx. your assignment submit word-lesson-8.docx . before submitting the document should contain a real heading 1. the hyperlink should have meaningful text. any informative image should have alt text. accessibility checker should have been reviewed. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 8.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 9
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 9 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 9 Spelling, Comments, and Track Changes Goal Practice reviewing a document using Word's spelling, comment, and revision tools. Instructions Create a new document. Type: This s
entries.text: word lesson 9 microsoft word lesson 9  word lesson 9 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 9 spelling, comments, and track changes goal practice reviewing a document using word's spelling, comment, and revision tools. instructions create a new document. type: this sentance contains a spelling mistake. press f7 to open editor or spelling and grammar review. correct sentance to sentence. type another paragraph containing at least two sentences. select one word or phrase. press ctrl+alt+m to create a comment. type: review this section. post the comment. press ctrl+shift+e to turn on track changes. add one word to the paragraph. delete one word. press ctrl+shift+e again to stop tracking new changes. use the review tab to inspect the tracked changes. accept one change. reject the other change. save as word-lesson-9.docx. your assignment submit word-lesson-9.docx . before submitting the spelling error should be corrected. the document should contain a comment. you should have practiced track changes. one change should have been accepted and one rejected. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 9.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Screen Reader Manual
entries.snippet: Microsoft Word Screen Reader Manual - Accessible Learning Center Skip to main content Microsoft Word Screen Reader Manual Narrator, NVDA, and JAWS Independent Self-Study Guide for Word on Windows Microsoft screen reader support for Word Pur
entries.text: microsoft word screen reader manual microsoft word screen reader manual  microsoft word screen reader manual - accessible learning center skip to main content microsoft word screen reader manual narrator, nvda, and jaws independent self-study guide for word on windows microsoft screen reader support for word purpose: this manual is written directly to a person learning microsoft word with a screen reader. it assumes little or no prior word experience and explains what to press, what should happen, what your screen reader should announce, and how to recover when the result is different. reference version: the manual is written primarily for word for microsoft 365 on windows. many commands also work in word 2024, 2021, 2019, and 2016, but ribbon wording can differ. screen readers: core word keyboard commands are taught first. narrator, nvda, and jaws are covered separately so screen-reader commands are not mixed together. how to use this manual work through parts 1-12 before focusing on your screen reader. those sections teach word itself. do one action, stop, and listen to what changed before pressing another key. word uses both direct shortcuts and the ribbon. direct shortcuts are usually faster once memorized. alt activates ribbon keytips. after pressing alt, use the letters word announces for the tab and command you want. f6 cycles among major word regions such as document, ribbon, status bar, and panes. tab and shift+tab move between controls in dialogs and panes. arrow keys move through text, menus, lists, and ribbon controls depending on context. narrator, nvda, and jaws all work with standard windows text-editing keys. use word's built-in styles instead of making headings look like headings only with bold and larger font. save often with ctrl+s. table of contents part 1 - what microsoft word is part 2 - open word and create a document part 3 - learn the word window and ribbon part 4 - type, move, select, and edit text part 5 - save, save as, open, and close part 6 - find and replace part 7 - character and paragraph formatting part 8 - headings, styles, and navigation pane part 9 - bulleted and numbered lists part 10 - tables part 11 - links, pictures, alt text, headers, and footers part 12 - spelling, grammar, and editor part 13 - comments part 14 - track changes part 15 - accessibility checker and accessible document design part 16 - print, export to pdf, and share part 17 - narrator with word part 18 - nvda with word part 19 - jaws with word part 20 - reading long documents part 21 - braille displays with word part 22 - word online part 23 - troubleshooting part 24 - independent practice course part 25 - quick reference commands part 26 - official microsoft resources part 1 - what microsoft word is microsoft word is a word-processing application for creating, reading, editing, formatting, reviewing, and sharing documents. word documents commonly use the docx format. document body: the main area where text is typed and edited. ribbon: a set of tabs such as home, insert, layout, references, review, and view. status bar: reports information such as page number, word count, and view. navigation pane: lets you search the document and move among headings. comments pane: contains collaboration comments. review features: track changes, accept/reject, comments, compare, spelling, and accessibility tools. part 2 - open word and create a document 2.1 open word from windows search what you will learn: start microsoft word without using a mouse. before you begin: word must be installed. exactly how to do it press the windows key. type word. use up/down arrow if more than one result appears. press enter on microsoft word. wait for word to open. what should happen: the word start screen or a document window opens. if that does not happen: if word does not appear in search, microsoft 365/word may not be installed or may use a different organization deployment. practice: open word twice using search. 2.2 create a blank document what you will learn: start a new editable document. before you begin: word is open. exactly how to do it press ctrl+n. wait for a blank document. type: this is my first word practice document. press enter twice. type a second sentence. what should happen: text appears in the new document. if that does not happen: if ctrl+n opens a start screen instead of a blank file, choose blank document with tab/enter. practice: create a new document and type two short paragraphs. part 3 - learn the word window and ribbon 3.1 move between word regions with f6 what you will learn: understand where keyboard focus is. before you begin: open a document. exactly how to do it press f6 once. listen to the region or control announced. press f6 again. continue several times. use shift+f6 to move backward through the regions. stop when focus returns to the document body. what should happen: focus cycles through word's major regions. if that does not happen: if f6 seems to do nothing, make sure word is the active application and no modal dialog is open. practice: cycle through all regions once. 3.2 use ribbon keytips what you will learn: reach a ribbon command by keyboard. before you begin: be in a word document. exactly how to do it press alt. listen for ribbon keytips. press h for home. listen as focus enters the home tab. use tab/shift+tab or arrow keys through controls. press escape to leave the ribbon and return toward the document. what should happen: the home ribbon tab becomes active. if that does not happen: if pressing alt opens an application menu from another program, word may not have focus. practice: open home, insert, and review tabs using alt key sequences. part 4 - type, move, select, and edit text task command character left/right left / right arrow word left/right ctrl+left / ctrl+right line up/down up / down arrow start/end of line home / end start/end of document ctrl+home / ctrl+end select character shift+left / shift+right select word ctrl+shift+left / ctrl+shift+right select line/paragraph portions shift with navigation keys select all ctrl+a delete previous character backspace delete next character delete undo ctrl+z redo/repeat ctrl+y 4.1 correct a typing error what you will learn: move the insertion point to an exact location and replace text. before you begin: type a sentence containing one deliberate error. exactly how to do it press ctrl+left arrow to move backward one word at a time. use left/right arrow to move one character at a time. press backspace or delete to remove the incorrect character. type the correct character. use your screen reader's line or word reading command to verify the correction. what should happen: the correction occurs at the intended position. if that does not happen: if text changes in the wrong location, press ctrl+home or ctrl+end to establish a known position and navigate again. practice: create three errors and correct all three. 4.2 select and replace a word what you will learn: select text with the keyboard. before you begin: place the caret next to a word. exactly how to do it hold ctrl+shift. press left or right arrow to select the word. release the keys. type the replacement word. what should happen: the selected word is replaced. if that does not happen: if extra punctuation or spaces are selected, undo with ctrl+z and select more carefully. practice: replace three words using selection. part 5 - save, save as, open, and close task command save ctrl+s save as f12 or ctrl+shift+s depending word version/configuration open ctrl+o close document ctrl+w exit word alt+f4 5.1 save a new document what you will learn: choose a filename and location. before you begin: have an unsaved document open. exactly how to do it press ctrl+s. if the save as area appears, navigate to the desired folder/location. move to the file name field. type a descriptive filename without typing .docx unless word requires it. move to save. press enter. wait for word to return to the document. what should happen: the document is saved as a docx file. if that does not happen: if word asks about another file format, choose docx unless you intentionally need another format. practice: save a practice document to documents. 5.2 reopen a saved document what you will learn: find and open an existing word file. before you begin: know the filename or recent location. exactly how to do it press ctrl+o. use the recent list or browse. navigate to the file. press enter. wait for the document to load. use ctrl+home and begin reading. what should happen: the correct document opens. if that does not happen: if another file opens, close it with ctrl+w and verify the filename before selecting. practice: close and reopen your practice file. part 6 - find and replace 6.1 find text what you will learn: search within a document. before you begin: open a document containing several paragraphs. exactly how to do it press ctrl+f. type the word or phrase you want to find. press enter if required. press tab until the results list is announced. use up/down arrow through results. press enter on a result to move to it. press escape to close the navigation pane when finished. what should happen: word moves to the selected occurrence. if that does not happen: if the navigation pane seems confusing, press escape and reopen with ctrl+f. practice: find three different words. 6.2 replace text what you will learn: replace one or all occurrences. before you begin: open a practice document. exactly how to do it press ctrl+h. type the old text in find what. press tab to replace with. type the new text. tab to find next and activate it. use replace to change only the current occurrence, or replace all only when every occurrence should change. read word's replacement count if shown. what should happen: the intended text is replaced. if that does not happen: if replace all would change unintended text, press escape and use replace one occurrence at a time. practice: replace one word safely, then undo. part 7 - character and paragraph formatting task command bold ctrl+b italic ctrl+i underline ctrl+u left align ctrl+l center ctrl+e right align ctrl+r justify ctrl+j increase font size ctrl+shift+> decrease font size ctrl+shift+< clear direct character formatting ctrl+spacebar 7.1 apply bold to existing text what you will learn: format selected text without retyping it. before you begin: have text available. exactly how to do it select the word or phrase. press ctrl+b. use your screen reader's formatting information command if available to confirm bold. press right arrow without shift to clear the selection and move the caret. what should happen: selected text becomes bold. if that does not happen: if newly typed text continues in bold unexpectedly, press ctrl+b again to toggle bold off. practice: bold and unbold a practice phrase. 7.2 change paragraph alignment what you will learn: change how a paragraph is positioned. before you begin: place the caret anywhere in a paragraph. exactly how to do it press ctrl+e to center. listen for any screen-reader formatting feedback. press ctrl+l to restore left alignment. what should happen: the paragraph alignment changes. if that does not happen: if only part of a paragraph changes unexpectedly, check whether text was selected. practice: center a heading, then restore left alignment. part 8 - headings, styles, and navigation pane built-in heading styles are critical for accessibility. they let screen readers and word's navigation pane understand document structure. task command heading 1 ctrl+alt+1 heading 2 ctrl+alt+2 heading 3 ctrl+alt+3 normal style ctrl+shift+n 8.1 apply a real heading style what you will learn: make a section navigable to screen readers. before you begin: type a short section title on its own line. exactly how to do it place the caret in the title line. press ctrl+alt+1 for heading 1, or ctrl+alt+2 for heading 2. move to the next paragraph and press ctrl+shift+n if you need to ensure normal style for body text. open navigation pane with ctrl+f. move to the headings view/ta word manual.html
